brief.headline: Rail-interdiction strike wave; Crimea declares emergency after drone barrage
brief.lead: Channels celebrated a coordinated Geran-drone campaign against Ukrainian railways and refineries while grappling with a record Ukrainian drone attack that forced Crimea and Sevastopol into an emergency regime and produced rare admissions of Ukrainian advances on the Zaporizhzhia front.

developments.title: Geran drones claimed to destroy five locomotives in rail-interdiction push
developments.body: Multiple channels amplified claims that Geran-2 drones destroyed five trains/locomotives at the Malynivka-Lozova hub on the Kharkiv-Zaporizhzhia border, framing it as a shift toward systematic railway interdiction. Rybar claimed increasing video confirmation of locomotive strikes; all figures are channel/MoD-sourced and unverified.

developments.title: Record Ukrainian drone attack forces Crimea emergency regime
developments.body: Channels reported a large Ukrainian drone strike on Crimea, Moscow, Tula and Vladimir regions, with Sevastopol power grid damage and a claimed 84 drones downed over Tula. Crimea and Sevastopol declared an emergency regime — described variously as security-driven and as a mechanism to accelerate federal budget aid. All casualty and interception figures unconfirmed.

developments.title: Rybar admits 'unfavorable dynamics' on Zaporizhzhia front
developments.body: Rybar reported Ukrainian forces advancing southward near Kamenske and Hulyaipole, allegedly occupying Primorske and pressuring Plavni — a rare negative frontline admission driving the topic's 29-point mood drop. Other channels countered with upbeat claims (Konstantinovka clearance, 763 structures/560+ soldiers per Kotsnews); numbers unverified.

developments.title: Prisoner exchange returns 160 Russian soldiers
developments.body: Channels widely reported a 160-for-160 prisoner swap with Ukraine, with Rybar claiming over 1,500 Russians returned since 2025. Framed positively with mentions of medical and rehabilitation support.

developments.title: Bloggers blame Rostechnadzor, private sector for refinery fires
developments.body: Two Majors and NgP raZVedka aired industry complaints that Rostechnadzor delays refinery security upgrades and that unclear federal-versus-private protection responsibility enables repeat Ukrainian strikes — a rare governance-critical thread amid claimed battlefield successes.

developments.title: Deep strikes claimed on Kyiv and Kremenchuk refinery
developments.body: Several channels reported combined missile-and-drone strikes on Kyiv, Poltava and the Kremenchuk refinery, citing secondary detonations as proof of hits. Notably, Rybar warned Russian media exaggerate fuel-infrastructure damage based on false Ukrainian claims about 150 fuel stations — an internal call for caution.

narrative_watch.title: Railway interdiction as new strike doctrine
narrative_watch.body: Channels are consolidating a frame that Russia has begun systematically targeting Ukrainian locomotives and rail hubs to choke logistics, presenting the Malynivka-Lozova strikes as a doctrinal shift rather than isolated hits.

narrative_watch.title: Domestic blame-shifting over refinery vulnerability
narrative_watch.body: A recurring thread pins repeat refinery/fuel strikes on Rostechnadzor delays and murky private-sector protection duties, deflecting from air-defense gaps while stopping short of criticizing top leadership.

narrative_watch.title: Societal atomization anxiety
narrative_watch.body: NgP raZVedka continues warning of weak civic solidarity, fuel hoarding and speculators undermining the home front, echoing a broader wartime-cohesion concern.

flag_texts.title: Frontline sentiment cools 29 points
flag_texts.body: Rybar's admission of 'unfavorable dynamics' and Ukrainian advances near Kamenske, Primorske and Hulyaipole pulled the frontline net score down to +62, tempering otherwise upbeat Konstantinovka and Red Liman claims.

flag_texts.title: Ukraine-strikes topic drops 35 points
flag_texts.body: A record Ukrainian drone attack on Crimea, Moscow, Tula and Vladimir regions — with Sevastopol grid damage and an emergency regime declared — drove sentiment to net -62.

flag_texts.title: West & NATO sentiment rebounds 29 points
flag_texts.body: Coverage of German F126 frigate cost overruns, a sympathetic Scott Ritter Donbas visit and Hormuz-Strait disruption lifted the topic's net to -21 despite Western aid concerns.

flag_texts.title: Mobilisation and Putin-criticism threads dormant
flag_texts.body: Watchlist items 'Mobilisation rumours' and 'Criticism of Putin' saw no substantive posts; governance criticism instead targeted Rostechnadzor and private-sector refinery protection, not the leadership directly.
